content: Before using famotidine, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to other H2 blockers (such as cimetidine or ranitidine), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. Some symptoms you experience may actually indicate a more serious underlying condition. During pregnancy, famotidine should only be used if it is clearly necessary. This medication passes into breast milk, so consult your doctor before breastfeeding. Drug interactions can alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs as well as herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Some medications require stomach acid for proper absorption. Since famotidine reduces stomach acid, it may affect how well these medications work. If someone overdoses and exhibits serious symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911) immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Lifestyle changes, such as participating in stress reduction programs, quitting smoking, limiting alcohol consumption, and making dietary adjustments (e.g., avoiding caffeine and certain spices), may enhance the effectiveness of this medication. Laboratory and/or medical tests, such as endoscopy or kidney function tests, may be performed while you are using this medication. Be sure to attend all medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose of this medication, it is important to take it as soon as possible. If you are unsure about what to do, consult your doctor or pharmacist for guidance on a new dosing schedule. For storage, refer to the product instructions or consult your pharmacist for specific details. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information was last revised in August 2024. It is important to note that this document is a summary and does not contain all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individualized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Side effects such as headache, constipation, diarrhea, or pain/redness at the injection site may occur. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefit to you outweighs the risk of side effects. A severe allergic reaction to this drug is rare, but seek immediate medical attention if it occurs. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects.
